claims.claim: currentChange is a percentage daily move (e.g., ~1.66 for USD), not an absolute NIS delta.
The Bank of Israel publishes a representative rate for exactly 14 currencies: USD, GBP, JPY, EUR, AUD, CAD, DKK, NOK, ZAR, SEK, CHF, JOD, LBP, EGP.
claims.raw_snippet: keys returned by the live endpoint: USD, GBP, JPY, EUR, AUD, CAD, DKK, NOK, ZAR, SEK, CHF, JOD, LBP, EGP (14 objects total).

claims.claim: Units vary by currency: JPY unit=100, LBP unit=10, most others unit=1.
The JSON endpoint's ?date= parameter is ignored: passing an old date still returns today's rate (lastUpdate unchanged).
claims.raw_snippet: GetExchangeRates?date=2026-01-01 and GetExchangeRates?date=2025-06-03 both return USD 2.872 with lastUpdate 2026-06-03T12:22:02Z (identical to the no-date response).

claims.claim: Historical rates come from the BOI SDMX EXR dataflow. Base path https://edge.boi.gov.il/FusionEdgeServer/sdmx/v2/data/dataflow/ ; series pattern https://edge.boi.gov.il/FusionEdgeServer/sdmx/v2/data/dataflow/BOI.STATISTICS/EXR/1.0/RER_<CUR>_ILS ; concrete example https://edge.boi.gov.il/FusionEdgeServer/sdmx/v2/data/dataflow/BOI.STATISTICS/EXR/1.0/RER_USD_ILS . With startPeriod, endPeriod and format=csv the response is a CSV whose columns include TIME_PERIOD and OBS_VALUE; read on 2026-08-11 the first 2026 USD observation is 2026-01-02 at 3.181 and the last in the window is 2026-01-15 at 3.156. Covers these references: https://edge.boi.gov.il/FusionEdgeServer/sdmx/v2/data/dataflow/BOI.STATISTICS/EXR/1.0/RER_USD_ILS?startPeriod=2026-01-01&endPeriod=2026-01-15&format=csv

claims.claim: The representative rate is published soon after 15:15 on regular days, and soon after 12:15 on Fridays, holiday eves and some other Jewish holidays. claims.claim: The Bank of Israel sets a single representative (average) rate, not separate buy/sell rates. The average rate in NIS is calculated on the basis of a sampling of exchange rates published by the banks on the Reuters screens (one unified representative rate, not separate buying/selling rates). The Bank of Israel web pages block automated fetching, so this is sourced to the Bank's own public exchange-rate API instead.
